what: Debounce waits until events stop (the user pauses typing) and then runs once; throttle runs at most once per time window while events keep coming (scroll, resize). Both stop a flood of events from causing a flood of work or network requests.
like: Debounce is the lift door that stays open while people keep stepping in; throttle is the turnstile that lets one person through every few seconds.
why: A typeahead sends one request per pause, not one per keystroke
Scroll and resize handlers don't block the main thread on every event
Fewer long tasks keeps interactions responsive (better INP)

steps.d: Typing, scroll, resize, mousemove and drag fire many events per second. Work per event adds up: network calls, layout reads, big re-renders.
Reset a timer on each event; run only after the user pauses for N ms. Ideal for search-as-you-type, autosave and form validation where only the last value matters.
Run at most once every N ms during the burst, optionally on the leading and trailing edge. Ideal for scroll position, resize, drag and analytics pings.

steps.t: Use a frame for visual work
steps.d: For visual updates, store the latest value in the handler and apply it in requestAnimationFrame, which runs once before each paint (about 60 times a second on a typical display).
Even after debouncing, an older response can arrive last. Use AbortController (or a query library) to cancel the previous request and ignore stale results.
useDeferredValue keeps the input urgent and re-renders the heavy list in the background, interruptibly. It does not reduce network requests, so combine it with debouncing for fetches.

numbers.l: A task longer than this is a long task; heavy work per event pushes handlers past it
Good INP threshold at the 75th percentile - keep handlers short enough to meet it
Typical display refresh rate, so rAF runs about 60 times a second (higher on 120 or 144 Hz screens)

tool: lodash, TanStack Pacer, RxJS, requestAnimationFrame, AbortController

choices.d: Debounce when only the final value matters (search, autosave). Throttle when you need updates during the action (scroll, drag, resize).
Short delay feels responsive but sends more requests; long delay feels laggy. Leading-edge runs immediately then ignores the rest; trailing-edge runs at the end. Pick by the UX, then measure.
Debounce/throttle limit how often you run (network, cheap logic). rAF aligns visual updates with paint. useDeferredValue adapts to device speed for render cost but does not cut requests.
A tiny debounce is easy, but cancellation, leading/trailing, flush and cleanup on unmount are easy to get wrong. Use a tested helper and clean up in the effect.

instead.why: Query keys already dedupe and cache repeated searches
Cancels in-flight requests when the input changes

breaks.d: Request for 'ab' returns after the request for 'abc', so results are out of order.
breaks.fix: AbortController, or key results by query and ignore anything not current

breaks.d: The timer fires after the component is gone and updates dead state.
breaks.see: Console warning or wrong data on the next page
breaks.fix: Cancel the timer in the cleanup function

breaks.d: Debounce delays the visible input update, not just the request.
breaks.see: Characters appear late in the field
breaks.fix: Keep the input controlled and instant; debounce only the side effect

say: I keep the input instant and debounce only the request, then abort the previous one, so a typeahead sends one call per pause and never shows out-of-order results.
For scroll and resize I throttle, or better, use IntersectionObserver or rAF, so handlers don't run more than once per frame.
If rendering is the bottleneck I reach for useDeferredValue, because it adapts to the device instead of using a fixed delay.

followups.a: Debounce adds a fixed delay and cuts requests. useDeferredValue has no fixed delay, is interruptible and helps slow renders, but still lets every keystroke fetch. They can be combined.

Scroll fires constantly and measuring layout inside it can force reflow. Prefer IntersectionObserver for visibility, CSS for sticky and scroll-snap, and rAF or throttle only when you truly need positions.

today: Fixed-delay timers are still right for cutting network calls, but React's useDeferredValue and transitions handle render cost, and the platform gives better tools than scroll listeners (IntersectionObserver, CSS scroll-driven animations, scheduler.yield for long work). INP has made handler cost a headline metric.

check.q: A search box should call the API only after the user pauses typing. Which technique?
check.why: Debounce waits for a quiet period and then runs once with the final value.

check.q: Which suits updating a header on scroll at a steady rate?
check.why: Throttle gives regular updates during the burst; debounce would wait until scrolling stops.

check.q: Why use AbortController with a debounced search?
check.a: To cancel the previous in-flight request so stale results don't win
check.why: Responses can return out of order; aborting avoids showing an old one.
